verses.sa: एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः । कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥
verses.tr: Even seekers of freedom acted after knowing this. Therefore, do the work that your ancestors always did.
verses.angle: purumukshubhi: seekers of freedom who still acted
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for a word that shows even those seeking freedom still did their work.

body.text: Even seekers of freedom acted after knowing this. Therefore, do the work that your ancestors always did. purumukshubhi means seekers of freedom, and Krishna names them to show that even those who seek freedom still do their work. Krishna now promises to explain the very nature of action and inaction.

verses.sa: किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः । तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥
verses.tr: What is action, and what is inaction? Even the wise are confused here. I will explain that action to you, knowing which you will be freed from what is harmful.
verses.angle: Kavayo, the wise, are deluded here
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just said that the wise are confused. Now he names the very problem that traps them, to show Arjuna that he alone has the answer.

body.text: What is action, and what is inaction? Even the wise are confused here. I will explain that action to you, knowing which you will be freed from what is harmful. The verse begins by naming kavayo, the wise, and stating that even they are mohita, deluded. Krishna does not hide the difficulty, but names it fully before offering the way out. Krishna now names action, forbidden action, and inaction to show that all three must be understood. Listen closely.

verses.sa: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः । अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥
verses.tr: Action, forbidden action, and inaction must all be understood, because the movement of action is hard to grasp.
verses.angle: Gahana: the hidden movement of karma
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna returns to the confusion about action and inaction, and adds a third term to the problem. Listen for the hidden nature of karma.

body.text: Action, forbidden action, and inaction must all be understood, because the movement of action is hard to grasp. Krishna names three things Arjuna must sort out: action, forbidden action and inaction, because karma moves in hidden ways. Krishna then shows the wise person who can see action within inaction and inaction within action.

verses.sa: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः । स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥
verses.tr: One who sees action in inaction, and inaction in action, is wise among people; that person is disciplined and complete in action.
verses.angle: Yuktah: inner discipline is the mark of wisdom
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: How can a person act without being bound by the action? Listen for the secret Krishna reveals about what it means to truly act.

body.text: One who sees action in inaction, and inaction in action, is wise among people; that person is disciplined and complete in action. The verse names one who sees action in inaction. That seer is called yuktah, disciplined and united, which means inner discipline is not the opposite of action, but the very mark of a wise person. Krishna next names the person who acts without desire, whose deeds are burned by the fire of knowledge.

verses.sa: यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः । ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥
verses.tr: The wise call that person learned whose actions begin without desire or personal planning, and whose deeds are burned by the fire of knowledge.
verses.angle: Wisdom burns up the binding force of deeds
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now names the person the wise truly respect. Listen for how knowledge itself acts on their deeds.

body.text: The wise call that person learned whose actions begin without desire or personal planning, and whose deeds are burned by the fire of knowledge. The verse gives us one exact image, the fire of knowledge burning up the person's deeds. This tells us that knowledge itself can consume the binding force of those deeds. Krishna then describes the one who has already dropped all craving and lives without dependence, even while acting.

verses.sa: त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः । कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥
verses.tr: One who has abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, remains ever content, and depends on nothing, does nothing at all even while fully engaged in action.
verses.angle: Abhipravritto api: fully engaged yet doing nothing
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now points to a person who is busy with work but does not do anything. Listen to the word that makes this possible.

body.text: One who has abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, remains ever content, and depends on nothing, does nothing at all even while fully engaged in action. Listen to the phrase abhipravritto api, even while fully engaged. Krishna is describing a person who is completely active, yet because they are without attachment and inner contentment, they do not perform any binding action. Krishna then explains that the person who gives up all hope and possessions is free from fault even while doing bodily work.

verses.sa: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः । शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verses.tr: One who has no hope, who has controlled the body and mind, and who has given up all possessions, does only bodily action and incurs no fault.
verses.angle: yatacittatma: the mind held in hand
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is teaching Arjuna how to act without being stained, even when the body is busy. Listen for the one who is fully in control.

body.text: One who has no hope, who has controlled the body and mind, and who has given up all possessions, does only bodily action and incurs no fault. Notice the word yatacittatma, one whose mind and inner being are controlled. This is a person whose mind is held in hand, so even ordinary bodily action leaves no trace of fault. Krishna adds that a person who is content with whatever comes, beyond opposites, is not bound even while acting.

verses.sa: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
verses.tr: Content with whatever comes by itself, beyond opposites, free from envy, equal in success and failure, such a person is not bound even while acting.
verses.angle: samah: the equal mind that stays unbound
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described a person who acts without hope of gain. Now he names the inner state that keeps a person unbound, even while doing work.

body.text: Content with whatever comes by itself, beyond opposites, free from envy, equal in success and failure, such a person is not bound even while acting. The word samah, equal, sits at the center. By staying equal in success and failure, a person stops the mind from tying itself to outcomes and stays free. Krishna then names the next quality, vimatsarah, freedom from envy, as the inner state that makes action clean.

verses.sa: गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः । यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते ॥
verses.tr: For one who has given up attachment, is freed, and whose mind rests in knowledge, all action melts away when done only for sacrifice.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks how to act without being trapped by the results, and here he gives a clear answer about what happens to a person's actions.

body.text: For one who has given up attachment, is freed, and whose mind rests in knowledge, all action melts away when done only for sacrifice. The word pragliyate means melts away, and it shows that for a person free of attachment and established in knowledge, all action simply disappears instead of remaining as a burden. Krishna then says that the offering itself is Brahman, and the person who sees it this way becomes one with Brahman.

verses.sa: ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् । ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥
verses.tr: In such sacrifice, the offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, and the act of offering into the fire of Brahman is Brahman. One whose action is absorbed in Brahman reaches Brahman alone.
verses.angle: Brahman is the offering, the fire, and the doer
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: On the battlefield, Krishna explains how to act without losing sight of the ultimate reality. Listen to how he dissolves every part of the sacrifice back into Brahman.

body.text: In such sacrifice, the offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, and the act of offering into the fire of Brahman is Brahman. One whose action is absorbed in Brahman reaches Brahman alone. The verse names every part of the sacrifice, and every part is Brahman. The offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, the fire is Brahman, and the one who offers is also Brahman. Krishna then shows two different paths of sacrifice that both lead to this same ultimate reality.

verses.sa: दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते । ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति ॥
verses.tr: Some yogis offer sacrifice to the divine alone. Others offer the self into the fire of Brahman through sacrifice itself.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is describing two paths of yoga. Listen for one word that appears twice, the word yajna, sacrifice.

body.text: Some yogis offer sacrifice to the divine alone. Others offer the self into the fire of Brahman through sacrifice itself. One word appears twice, yajna, sacrifice, binding both lines of action together. In the first line, the offering goes to the divine alone, while in the second, the offering is the self into the fire of Brahman. The next verse will describe yet another way yogis offer their senses into the fire of restraint.

verses.sa: श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति । शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥
verses.tr: Some yogis offer the senses into the fires of restraint. Others offer sound and the other sense-objects into the fires of the senses.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna explains to Arjuna how to train the mind using a Vedic fire sacrifice. Listen for the two different offerings.

body.text: Some yogis offer the senses into the fires of restraint. Others offer sound and the other sense-objects into the fires of the senses. Krishna uses the word others, anye, to mark a sharp turn. He is describing two different yogis and their two different fires. Sanjaya will now describe the army formations, beginning with Duryodhana's actions.

verses.sa: सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे । आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते ॥
verses.tr: Others offer all the activities of the senses and the life-force into the fire of self-control, lit by knowledge.
verses.angle: Knowledge kindles the fire of self-control
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has shown many ways to sacrifice. Now he speaks of a deeper fire. Listen for who offers what into it.

body.text: Others offer all the activities of the senses and the life-force into the fire of self-control, lit by knowledge. Listen to the role of knowledge here. It is knowledge that kindles the fire of self-control, and into that flame they offer every activity of the senses and the life-force. Krishna then names the material offerings others make, from wealth to study, as a further form of sacrifice.

verses.tr: Others offer wealth, austerity, yoga, and the study of sacred texts as sacrifice, while disciplined seekers make these offerings with firm vows.
verses.angle: Firm vows make any offering a true sacrifice
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: If sacrifice is not just ritual, what else can it be? Listen to how the text names four different offerings that people make.

body.text: Others offer wealth, austerity, yoga, and the study of sacred texts as sacrifice, while disciplined seekers make these offerings with firm vows. The verse lists four paths, wealth, austerity, yoga, and study, and it calls all of them yajnas. The key is not the offering itself, but that these are done by disciplined seekers with firm vows. Krishna then turns to the breath itself, showing how even the movement of air can become a sacrifice.
